compiled_state.title: [suggestion-record.sh]: env var CLAUDE_SESSION_ID never set by runtime -> session ID always falls through to random UUID
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview
Discovered during investigation of fe66-f05b (cross-session PR ownership). plugins/dso/scripts/suggestion-record.sh lines 127-128 read \`CLAUDE_SESSION_ID\` from the environment as the session-ID fallback, but the Claude Code runtime sets \`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID\` (different variable name). The elif branch was therefore dead code: every suggestion record was being written with a random UUID rather than the actual session ID, breaking the per-session correlation that suggestion analytics depend on.

## Expected Behavior
\`suggestion-record.sh\` should read the canonical Claude Code runtime variable \`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID\` so that suggestion records correlate with the originating session.

## Actual Behavior
Reading \`CLAUDE_SESSION_ID\` (unset by runtime) -> always falls through to the random-UUID generator -> every session-record gets a fresh UUID -> session correlation lost.

## Fix
One-file edit: read \`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID\` (the runtime contract). The dead \`CLAUDE_SESSION_ID\` branch is removed entirely (no backwards-compat shim — the variable was never populated by any caller).

## Related
Discovered while planning fe66-f05b (cross-session PR ownership tracking). The variable name surfaced when the design called for stamping a session ID into PR bodies and we empirically confirmed the runtime contract.
